posts.title: A NATION OF IMMIGRANTS
posts.description: “A Nation of Immigrants,” that old cliché! And yet it applies . . . to architecture. American architecture was transformed, the story goes, by Bauhaus émigrés who fled Nazi Germany. True enough, but less obvious is that many—most—of the leading figures of the postwar decades were also architects who came from elsewhere, not necessarily Germany. posts.title: BODYWORK
posts.description: I’ve not visited the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, but I have read that its skin is made of fiberglass-reinforced polymer. Beneath the biomorphic forms are the hidden bones of structural steel. Sort of like the human body, you might say.
